title: Lift-off SDK checklist + telemetry manifest (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic draft for a "lift-off" developer path for new SDK adopters. The goal is a 5-step lightweight flow that gets an engineer from signup -> sample app -> instrumented telemetry and to a first successful call in under 20 minutes.

Audience:
- Product engineers integrating Redwood APIs for the first time
- SEs running quick pilots with customers
- Internal bootcamp instructors who need a minimal reproducible demo

Constraints / design principles:
- Keep cognitive load low: one path that works end-to-end (happy path) before branching into advanced options
- Telemetry-first: every quickstart should include a minimal telemetry manifest so customers see usage and cost signals from minute one
- Language-agnostic samples (JS + Python, but single-file examples)
- No infra required: use hosted API and a tiny local server for callbacks if needed

Lift-off flow (five steps, concise):
1) Account + API key: short checklist (verify billing, region selection, basic quota)
2) Clone sample repo: `git clone github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter && cd sdk-starter`
3) Install & run minimal example (JS): `npm i && NODE_ENV=dev node examples/lift-off.js` — default prints generation stream and token cost estimate
4) Wire telemetry: copy `telemetry-manifest.json` into repo, run `node tools/telemetry-smoke.js` to emit events to the sandbox collector
5) Inspect console/console.redwood: see per-token latency, cost, and sample trace; validate output quality against the example prompts

Minimal SDK example (JS, single file):
(placed in examples/lift-off.js in repo)
- imports: `import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk'`
- call: `await redwood.chat.create({model: 'rwd-std-1', messages: [...]})`
- prints token counts + time-to-first-byte + inference-id for trace linking

Telemetry manifest (minimal required fields):
- event: sdk.init (api_key_hash, sdk_version, lang)
- event: request.sent (timestamp, model, route, prompt_hash, estimated_tokens)
- event: response.received (timestamp, inference_id, latency_ms, actual_tokens, status)
- event: cost.estimate (request_id, estimated_usd)
Notes: manifest should be a file users can drop into the sample repo. Collector is sandbox-only in the quickstart; production wiring covered in separate doc.

Preflight checklist for DX team (internal):
- [ ] Example repo builds in CI for Node 18 and Python 3.11
- [ ] Telemetry smoke harness added to PRs
- [ ] Quickstart page includes single animated gif showing 20-min path
- [ ] Error messages include clear remediation steps (auth, region, rate limit)

Acceptance criteria for a successful lift-off:
- user runs example and sees a generated message + token/cost lines in <20 minutes
- telemetry events appear in the sandbox console and are linkable to the inference trace
- README has one troubleshooting section with three top failures and commands to fix them

Edge / extras (optional sections to add later):
- Canary branch that swaps model to quantized variant when latency > X ms
- Local-mode runner for devs wanting no network dependency (uses small LLM shim)
- Mini-check to show batching benefits: run 10 parallel prompts and compare per-token cost

Open questions / TODOs:
- Which exact telemetry fields are PII-safe (we should avoid storing prompt text in telemetry by default)? Owner: Claire Z.
- Do we prefer `sdk.init` to be auto-emitted inside the constructor or explicit in examples? Trade-off: simplicity vs. surprise in production events. Owner: Miguel S.
- Do we include an integration example that uses Dedicated routing policy? Might be confusing in quickstart. Owner: Aisha K.

Notes to self (drafty):
- Keep wording conversational: "Run one command" > "Follow the instructions below"
- GIF should show dev running example, opening console, clicking a trace, seeing cost breakdown

Next steps / small backlog (first 6 weeks):
- Week 1: polish example code and telemetry manifest; add CI smoke tests (owner: Benji)
- Week 2: craft one-pager landing doc for onboarding flow (owner: Aisha)
- Week 3: record 60s walkthrough GIF + slate for docs site (owner: Claire)
- Week 4: publish sample repo, link from quickstart site, set up feedback collector (owner: Miguel)

Links / references:
- GH starter: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter (internal)
- Related Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-UI/SDK-ONRAMP-1234
- Telemetry spec (WIP): GH: redwood-inference/telemetry-spec#12

If you use this doc: please leave comments inline in the sample repo PR and ping me in #devexp.

-- end of draft --
